entities.summary: John Samuel Vander Meer was an American professional baseball player. He played in Major League Baseball as a left-handed pitcher, most prominently as a member of the Cincinnati Reds, where he became the only pitcher in Major League Baseball history to throw two consecutive no-hitters, an accomplishment which has long been considered to be impossible to replicate. He was a member of the 1940 World Series winning team. After the impressive start to his major league career, he experienced problems controlling the accuracy of his pitching, and his later career was marked by inconsistent performances.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Johnny Vander Meer's achievement of throwing two consecutive no-hitters in Major League Baseball history has been recognized as one of the most impressive feats in baseball, and his impact on the sport continues to be celebrated by fans and players alike.
